title: Man. Post. Cap. VII: PLAC Gen 3 sentence ≠ stripping justice; ≠ morte morieris
pass_a_gloss: Placeus grants the Gen. 3 sentence stands, but asks what follows. Can GAR show any Scripture judicial sentence by which Adam was stripped of justice? He will not grant that the Gen. 3:16–17 penalties on Eve and Adam were what the law chiefly threatened by dying you shall die—that fights Christ's satisfaction and the faithful's full justification on account of it.
pass_b_english: PLAC. That I indeed confess: for that sentence in Gen. 3 stands. But what follows from it? Can the learned man show in Scripture any judicial sentence of God by which Adam was stripped of justice? And yet I do not assent to the learned man that the penalties inflicted on Eve and Adam by the sentence given in Gen. 3:16–17 were those which the law chiefly threatened by the words dying you shall die. For that fights with Christ's satisfaction, and with the full and perfect justification of the faithful on account of it.
source_text: PLAC. Id equidem fateor: Extat enim illa sententia Gen. 3. Sed quid inde sequitur? Potestne ostendere vir doctus in Scriptura judiciariam aliquam Dei sententiam, qua fuerit Adamus spoliatus justitia? Et tamen non assentior viro docto poenas sententia lata Gen. 3. 16. 17. Evae & Adamo irrogatas, eas fuisse, quas lex praecipue comminabatur verbis morte morieris. Id enim pugnat cum Christi satisfactione, & fidelium propter eam justificatione plena & perfecta.

choices.choice: Gen 3 sentence ≠ strip justice; Gen 3:16–17 ≠ morte morieris (Christ)
